name: SparkFun Qwiic PIR (170 uA, EKMC4607112K)
description: Passive infrared motion sensor (Panasonic EKMC4607112K, 170 uA, digital output, detects people up to about 5-7 m) read over I2C through an ATtiny84 running SparkFun's Qwiic PIR firmware: it reports the live PIR output, debounced object-detected/removed events, time-stamped event queues and an active-low INT line. 3.3 V board with 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups. I2C address 0x12 (0x13 with the ADR jumper cut, or set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic PIR - 170uA (EKMC4607112K) (SEN-17374), 5-pin 0.1" header INT, SCL, SDA, 3V3, GND plus two Qwiic connectors.
eli5: Notices when a warm body like a person moves in front of it and tells your board over two wires.

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, active low (driven low by the ATtiny when an event is waiting and interrupts are enabled), 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board. Not needed for basic use

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (no regulator on the board; the Qwiic system is 3.3 V only)

buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: the board has no regulator and its I2C pull-ups go to its own 3V3 pin. The EKMC4607112K needs at least 3.0 V.
After power-up the PIR output is undefined for up to 30 s (circuit stability time); ignore readings until then.
Register reads: write the register number, then read; 16- and 32-bit registers are little-endian. Register 0x00 must read 0x72.
Status register 0x03: bit 0 = live PIR output, bit 1 = new event, bit 2 = object removed, bit 3 = object detected; write the byte back with bits 1-3 cleared to clear the events.
Default address 0x12; cutting the ADR jumper gives 0x13. A software-set address (register 0x19) is kept in EEPROM.
INT is only needed for interrupt-driven code; it is active low with a 10 kΩ pull-up on the board.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_pir import QwiicPIR

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
pir = QwiicPIR(i2c)
print('ID=0x%02X' % pir.device_id())
# The EKMC4607112K needs up to 30 s after power-up before its output is valid.
events = 0
last = None
while True:
    m = pir.raw_reading()
    if m != last:
        if m:
            events += 1
            print('MOTION %d' % events)
        else:
            print('CLEAR %d' % events)
        last = m
    time.sleep_ms(100)
